subject: In mice, briefly disrupting body-position sense caused navigation errors
script: From Agewell Brief: In mice, briefly disrupting body-position sense caused navigation errors. A new study in mice finds that temporarily disrupting proprioception—the sense of body position—causes subtle navigation errors, offering a fresh window into how the brain builds spatial memory. Researchers used light to briefly quiet proprioception in mice. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
